note: 'A termo certo' means for a fixed period; its opposite is 'sem termo', a permanent contract.

context: O diretor assinou o despacho esta manhã.
gapped: The director signed the ___ this morning.
note: A 'despacho' is an official written order or ruling from someone in authority, not a 'dispatch' in the courier sense.

context: Vou entregar o relatório amanhã de manhã.
gapped: I'm going to ___ the report tomorrow morning.
note: 'Entregar' is to hand something over or in; the reflexive 'entregar-se' means to give yourself up.

hints.similar: the last syllable sounds like "gar" in "guitar"

context: Tenho uma entrevista de emprego amanhã de manhã.
gapped: I have a ___ tomorrow morning.
note: 'Entrevista' alone already means interview; 'de emprego' makes it the job-hunting kind.

context: Deixei os documentos no escritório.
gapped: I left the documents at the ___.
note: 'Escritório' is the place you work; 'secretária' is the desk you sit at.

hints.similar: the ending sounds like the "-story" in "history"

context: A empresa contratou um estagiário para o verão.
gapped: The company hired an ___ for the summer.
note: In British English people often say 'trainee' or 'work placement'.

context: A empresa dá formação aos novos funcionários.
gapped: The company gives ___ to new employees.
note: 'Formação' is training or a course; 'formation' is about forming something.

context: Os maquinistas estão em greve desde terça-feira.
gapped: The train drivers have been on ___ since Tuesday.
note: 'Em greve' is 'on strike' — nothing to do with 'grief'.

context: Fiz horas extras todos os dias esta semana.
gapped: I did ___ every day this week.
note: 'Horas extras' is usually 'overtime' in English, which is uncountable; 'extra hours' is also possible but less specific.

context: A Ana está de licença de maternidade até setembro.
gapped: Ana is on ___ until September.
note: 'Licença' here is time off work, not a licence; a driving licence is 'carta de condução'.

hints.similar: the middle of "licença" sounds like English "sense"

context: Tens de marcar o ponto quando chegas à fábrica.
gapped: You have to ___ when you get to the factory.
note: 'Marcar o ponto' is to clock in or out with a time clock.

context: A ordem de trabalhos da reunião tem cinco pontos.
gapped: The ___ for the meeting has five items.
note: It's the list of things to discuss; 'agenda' in Portuguese is a diary.

context: O patrão quer falar comigo no fim do dia.
gapped: The ___ wants to talk to me at the end of the day.
note: 'Patrão' is your boss or employer; an English 'patron' is a customer or sponsor.

hints.similar: sounds like "pa-trown", close to English "brown" with a nasal

context: Faço sempre uma pausa para o almoço de uma hora.
gapped: I always take an hour's ___.
note: 'Pausa' is a break or pause, but English says 'lunch break', never 'pause for lunch'.

context: Não vamos conseguir cumprir o prazo deste trabalho.
gapped: We're not going to be able to meet the ___ for this job.
note: 'Prazo' is a deadline or time limit — never a school 'term'.

context: Deram-me uma promoção no mês passado.
gapped: They gave me a ___ last month.
note: In shops a 'promoção' is a special offer or sale; at work it's the step up the ladder.

hints.similar: the last syllable sounds like English "sown"

context: O relatório mensal tem de estar pronto na segunda.
gapped: The monthly ___ has to be ready on Monday.
note: 'Relatório' is the report; a 'relator' is a rapporteur, not a reporter.

context: Assinámos a rescisão do contrato na semana passada.
gapped: We signed the ___ of the contract last week.
note: In everyday speech people just say the contract was ended or terminated.

context: A reunião de equipa ficou marcada para as dez.
gapped: The team ___ was set for ten o'clock.
note: 'Reunião' is any meeting; a 'reunion' is a 'reencontro' of old friends.

context: Pus os papéis em cima da secretária.
gapped: I put the papers on the ___.
note: The piece of furniture is 'secretária', and a female secretary is also 'secretária' — only context tells them apart.

context: Faço teletrabalho dois dias por semana.
gapped: I do ___ two days a week.
note: In everyday English people say 'working from home' or 'WFH'.

context: Trabalho a tempo inteiro numa empresa de software.
gapped: I work ___ at a software company.
note: 'A tempo inteiro' is full-time; Brazilians say 'em tempo integral'.

context: Esta semana calha-me o turno da noite.
gapped: This week I'm on the night ___.
note: A 'turno' is a work shift; your 'turn' in a queue is a 'vez'.

context: O vencimento é pago no dia vinte e cinco.
gapped: The ___ is paid on the twenty-fifth.
note: 'Vencimento' here is your monthly pay; in other contexts it means a due date.
